# CycloDesk

[![Lifecycle:
alpha](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-alpha-orange.svg)](https://github.com/stratigraphy/CycloDesk/blob/main/NEWS.md)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/stratigraphy/CycloDesk/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/stratigraphy/CycloDesk/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.23983505.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23983505)
[![License: GPL (\>=
2)](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL%20(%3E%3D%202)-blue.svg)](https://stratigraphy.github.io/CycloDesk/LICENSE.md)

**A point-and-click workbench for cyclostratigraphy and paleoclimate
time series, built on R.**

CycloDesk puts the R packages
[WaverideR](https://github.com/stratigraphy/WaverideR) and
[astrochron](https://cran.r-project.org/package=astrochron) behind menus
and buttons, together with empirical mode decomposition from
[DecomposeR](https://cran.r-project.org/package=DecomposeR), the
Lomb-Scargle periodogram and dynamic time warping. Open a folder with
your data, pick a tool, press Run: spectra, wavelets, filters, cycle
tracking, age models, tuning, TimeOpt and COCO, without writing code.
Every step writes its result as a plain text file next to your data and
records the equivalent R code, so anything you click can be repeated in
a script.

It runs on your own computer, in its own window: your data never leave
your machine.

The interface is available in **English, French, Dutch, German, Spanish
and Chinese** (Help \> Language); corrections and further languages are
welcome: each language is [one text
file](https://stratigraphy.github.io/CycloDesk/inst/i18n/README.md).

> **Status: alpha.** CycloDesk works and is being used for real records,
> but menus, defaults and file names may still change. Please
> [report](https://github.com/stratigraphy/CycloDesk/issues/new/choose)
> anything that breaks, looks wrong or is confusing. Feedback now shapes
> the first stable release.

![CycloDesk: tracking a cycle on the wavelet scalogram, with the
extracted cycle, floating age model and tuned series
below](reference/figures/05_track.png)

CycloDesk: tracking a cycle on the wavelet scalogram, with the extracted
cycle, floating age model and tuned series below

## What it does

| Menu | Tools |
|----|----|
| **File / Plot** | Working-folder browser (drives, places, drag-and-drop), text, csv, Excel and LAS files; overlay, stacked and standardised plots, zoom, data table, sampling rate, data distribution |
| **Basic Series** | Make or load a series: astronomical solutions (La2004, La2010, La2011), insolation series and maps, ETP, the Imbrie ice-volume model; synthetic records (signal and noise generators, sedimentation-rate ramps, synthetic stratigraphy, bioturbation); example data |
| **Processing** | Prepare the data: sorting, selecting/removing parts (draggable lines), outliers, clipping; interpolation (also Laepple-Huybers for uneven records) and resampling; transformations, derivative, smoothing, tapers; detrending and pre-whitening; statistics, moving-window statistics and correlation, PCA, peaks; Bayesian change points |
| **Time Series** | Spectra (MTM, LOWSPEC, MESA, AMTM, SWA, Lomb-Scargle, Bayesian) with peak tests; evolutive spectra; wavelets (22 mother wavelets), superlets, synchrosqueezing and chirp-matched transforms; significance tests and surrogates; filtering, Hilbert amplitude and cycle extraction; coherence, cross wavelet and cross-spectral phase; EMD/EEMD and SSA (DecomposeR); bispectra, bicoherence, recurrence plots; rho1, DYNOT, PDA, spectral moments |
| **Sed. rate** | Tracking a cycle or a rate (by hand, astronomical HMM, chirp-steered, MESA ridge, FLMW); TimeOpt, eTimeOpt and windowed TimeOpt, with Monte Carlo significance, templates and Bayesian versions; COCO/eCOCO, cross-validated and adaptive; ASM/eASM and other astronomical tests |
| **Age models** | Building an age model (from a cycle, a sedimentation rate, minimal tuning, tie points) and tuning; anchoring to absolute ages (astronomical solution, anchorTime, weighted mean ages, the geological time scale); Bchron and astroMCBchron; Monte Carlo uncertainty and gap durations; checks of an age model; correlation by dynamic time warping |
| **Astronomy** | Astronomical periods at any age and through time, term identification, bundling ratios, tones, chaotic resonance; CTest and the precession constant, tests of tuned records; the Earth-Moon system |
| **Track** | Track a cycle on any scalogram or evolutive spectrum (wavelet, superlet, SST, EHA, MESA) or a sedimentation rate on an eTimeOpt or eCOCO map: snap to peaks or free points, HMM ridge following, LOWESS smoothing, helper lines for other cycles, floating age model, extraction of any cycle, tuning check against the amplitude modulation |
| **Anchor** | Tie a floating record to an astronomical solution, insolation or a metronome by clicking matching peaks |
| **Image** | A colour and brightness record (grey, L\*a\*b\*, RGB, HSV) along a route clicked on an outcrop photograph, core scan, tree-ring image or satellite image |

The menus and the five tabs follow the order of the work: **Data**,
**Plot**, **Processing**, **Analysis & age models** and **R code &
log**. Each menu opens submenus by subject. The Processing tab lists the
tools that make and prepare a series, the Analysis & age models tab
those for time-series analysis, sedimentation rates, age models and
astronomy, each with a search box; Track, Anchor and Image open as views
inside these two tabs. The file panel can be widened, or collapsed to a
ribbon; right-click a file to plot, rename, duplicate or delete it.

Every figure of a tool can be zoomed (drag a box or type the limits) to
read off a spectral peak, and sliding-window analyses can be padded so
their result spans the whole record. Heavy calculations run in a
separate R process, so the window stays usable and can cancel them. The
**R code & log** tab collects the code of every step; **Help \> Which R
function does what** lists the function behind each menu.

|  |  |
|----|----|
| ![Spectral analysis](reference/figures/03_spectrum.png) | ![Wavelet analysis](reference/figures/04_wavelet.png) |
| Spectral analysis with confidence levels | Wavelet scalogram with average spectrum |
| ![Tuning check](reference/figures/06_check.png) | ![Anchoring](reference/figures/07_anchor.png) |
| Tuning check: envelope of a cycle against the modulating cycle | Anchoring a floating record to La2004 |

## Installation

### Installer: download, double-click, done (Windows, macOS, Linux)

Download the installer for your computer from the [**latest
release**](https://github.com/stratigraphy/CycloDesk/releases/latest).
It contains its own copy of R and all packages, so you do not need R,
and it does not change an R you may already have. No administrator
rights are needed.

| Computer | File | How |
|----|----|----|
| Windows 10/11 | `CycloDesk-<version>-Windows-x86_64.exe` | Double-click and follow the steps. Windows may first say “Windows protected your PC”: click *More info* \> *Run anyway* (the installer is not yet code-signed). |
| Mac with Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `CycloDesk-<version>-MacOSX-arm64.pkg` | Double-click. If macOS says it cannot check the developer, right-click (Control-click) the file and choose *Open*, or allow it under *System Settings \> Privacy & Security*. |
| Mac with an Intel processor | `CycloDesk-<version>-MacOSX-x86_64.pkg` | As above. |
| Linux (x86_64) | `CycloDesk-<version>-Linux-x86_64.sh` | In a terminal: `bash CycloDesk-<version>-Linux-x86_64.sh`. The window needs WebKitGTK 4.1 (standard on Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora); without it CycloDesk opens in the web browser. |

Afterwards, start **CycloDesk** from the desktop icon, the Start menu,
Applications/Launchpad or the applications menu. It opens in its own
window; your data stay on your computer. CycloDesk checks once a day
whether a newer version of CycloDesk or WaverideR is available and
offers to install it (*Update and restart*).

To remove it: Windows, *Settings \> Apps*; macOS, delete
`~/Library/CycloDesk` and *CycloDesk* in Applications; Linux, delete the
`CycloDesk` folder in your home folder.

### From R (Windows, macOS, Linux)

``` r

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("stratigraphy/WaverideR")   # always the newest WaverideR
remotes::install_github("stratigraphy/CycloDesk")
CycloDesk::run_app()                                # or run_app("path/to/your/data")
```

Both packages are pure R; no compilers or Rtools are needed. The
optional tools also use the CRAN packages DecomposeR, lomb and dtw.

### Windows launcher for an existing R

If you already use R on Windows,
[CycloDesk-launcher.zip](https://github.com/stratigraphy/CycloDesk/releases/latest/download/CycloDesk-launcher.zip)
installs CycloDesk into that R: unzip it somewhere permanent
(e.g. `Documents\Apps`), double-click **SETUP.bat**, then use the
desktop icon.

## Getting started

The
[tutorial](https://stratigraphy.github.io/CycloDesk/articles/getting-started.html)
walks through a complete analysis of the IODP Site 926 grey-scale record
that comes with WaverideR: spectrum, wavelet, tracking the eccentricity
cycle, a floating age model, the tuning check and anchoring to La2004.

## Feedback and help

- **Something broken or wrong?** [Open a bug
  report](https://github.com/stratigraphy/CycloDesk/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml).
- **Missing a method or an idea for the interface?** [Suggest a
  feature](https://github.com/stratigraphy/CycloDesk/issues/new?template=feature_request.yml).
- **Questions, or want to show what you did with it?** Use the
  [Discussions](https://github.com/stratigraphy/CycloDesk/discussions).

Contributions are welcome; see
[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://stratigraphy.github.io/CycloDesk/CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Citation

If CycloDesk helps your work, please cite it, together with the packages
that do the calculations:

- Arts, M. (2026). CycloDesk: Graphical Interface for Cyclostratigraphy.
  R package version 0.2.2. <https://github.com/stratigraphy/CycloDesk>
- Arts, M., Corradini, C., Pondrelli, M., Pas, D., Da Silva, A.-C.
  (2024). Age and orbital forcing in the upper Silurian Cellon section
  (Carnic Alps, Austria) uncovered using the WaverideR R package.
  Frontiers in Earth Science 12, 1357751.
  <https://doi.org/10.3389/feart.2024.1357751>
- Arts, M. (2023). WaverideR: Extracting Signals from Wavelet Spectra. R
  package. <https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=WaverideR>
- Meyers, S.R. (2014). Astrochron: An R Package for Astrochronology.
  <https://cran.r-project.org/package=astrochron>

plus the papers of the methods you used (listed in each tool’s help
panel). In R: `citation("CycloDesk")`.

## Acknowledgements

The menu layout and the working-folder workflow are inspired by
[Acycle](https://github.com/mingsongli/acycle) (Li, Hinnov and Kump,
2019, Computers & Geosciences 127, 12-22,
<https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cageo.2019.02.011>). CycloDesk contains no
Acycle code; all calculations are done by WaverideR, astrochron and the
other R packages named above.

# Package index

## Start the interface

- [`run_app()`](https://stratigraphy.github.io/CycloDesk/reference/run_app.md)
  : Start the CycloDesk interface
- [`cd_app()`](https://stratigraphy.github.io/CycloDesk/reference/cd_app.md)
  : The CycloDesk Shiny application object

## Reading and writing data files

- [`read_series()`](https://stratigraphy.github.io/CycloDesk/reference/read_series.md)
  : Read a data series file
- [`write_series()`](https://stratigraphy.github.io/CycloDesk/reference/write_series.md)
  : Write a data series file
- [`cd_pad_ends()`](https://stratigraphy.github.io/CycloDesk/reference/cd_pad_ends.md)
  : Pad a series at both ends
- [`cd_image_profile()`](https://stratigraphy.github.io/CycloDesk/reference/cd_image_profile.md)
  : Colour and brightness record along a route on an image

## Astronomical solutions, tracking and age models

- [`cd_laskar()`](https://stratigraphy.github.io/CycloDesk/reference/cd_laskar.md)
  : Astronomical solution with a local cache
- [`cd_insolation()`](https://stratigraphy.github.io/CycloDesk/reference/cd_insolation.md)
  : Daily mean insolation from the La2004 solution
- [`cd_snap_track()`](https://stratigraphy.github.io/CycloDesk/reference/cd_snap_track.md)
  : Snap a tracked curve to the nearest power peaks
- [`cd_cycle_agemodel()`](https://stratigraphy.github.io/CycloDesk/reference/cd_cycle_agemodel.md)
  : Age model from a filtered cycle

## Package

- [`CycloDesk`](https://stratigraphy.github.io/CycloDesk/reference/CycloDesk-package.md)
  [`CycloDesk-package`](https://stratigraphy.github.io/CycloDesk/reference/CycloDesk-package.md)
  : CycloDesk: a point-and-click interface for cyclostratigraphy
